title: The Stunning Rise of the Democratic Socialists of America

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·荣森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 即使是在我还在夜店里用黑胶唱片打碟的那个年代，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你每天晚上都要带着300件最珍贵的宝贝去工作，把DJ台变成了一个充满活力的快闪博物馆，陈列着那些精美的、有50年历史的艺术品。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼出品的《重构者》吧。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴尔巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: This summer, Democratic Socialists have mounted their biggest and most successful attempt yet to redefine the Democratic Party.
sentences.zh: 今年夏天，民主社会主义者发起了迄今为止规模最大、也最成功的一次尝试，旨在重新定义民主党。

sentences.en: 48 hours after Democratic Socialists won in two New York congressional districts, the implications are still being felt and this really could just be the start.
sentences.zh: 在民主社会主义者赢得纽约两个国会选区席位48小时后，其影响仍在持续发酵，而这可能仅仅是个开始。

sentences.en: By defeating its candidates in primary after primary from the East CoaSt.
sentences.zh: 通过在东海岸一场又一场的初选中击败民主党的候选人。

sentences.en: Janice Lewis-George is poised to become the first Democratic Socialist mayor in the history of the nation's capital.
sentences.zh: 贾妮斯·刘易斯-乔治有望成为美国首都历史上首位民主社会主义者市长。

sentences.en: To the West CoaSt.
sentences.zh: 再到西海岸。

sentences.en: Democratic Socialists scored another primary victory, this time in Colorado's first congressional district.
sentences.zh: 民主社会主义者又赢得了一场初选，这次是在科罗拉多州的第一国会选区。

sentences.en: To swing states.
sentences.zh: 再到摇摆州。

sentences.en: Democrat Socialists won several races, notably in Michigan.
sentences.zh: 民主社会主义者赢得了几场竞选，特别是在密歇根州。

sentences.en: Chris Rapp, the Democratic Party's nominee in the third district of Pennsylvania, is also a member of the Democratic Socialists of America.
sentences.zh: 克里斯·拉普，这位民主党在宾夕法尼亚州第三选区的提名人，也是美国民主社会主义者协会的成员。

sentences.en: And finally, to the heart of red America.
sentences.zh: 最后，来到红色美国的心脏地带。

sentences.en: Let's talk Florida.
sentences.zh: 我们来谈谈佛罗里达州。

sentences.en: Democratic Socialist Angie Nixon crushed Alex Vindman.
sentences.zh: 民主社会主义者安吉·尼克松击败了亚历克斯·温德曼。

sentences.en: In the process, Americans' views of Democratic Socialists and socialism itself are changing.
sentences.zh: 在此过程中，美国人对民主社会主义者以及社会主义本身的看法正在发生改变。

sentences.en: Socialism up like a rocket.
sentences.zh: 社会主义的支持率像火箭一样蹿升。

sentences.en: Look at this.
sentences.zh: 看看这个。

sentences.en: Two in three Democrats have a favorable view of socialism.
sentences.zh: 三分之二的民主党人对社会主义持正面看法。

sentences.en: Related to CBS News poll found Democrats view socialism more favorably than capitalism.
sentences.zh: 哥伦比亚广播公司新闻部的一项相关民调发现，民主党人对社会主义的看法比对资本主义更正面。

sentences.en: Democratic Socialists of America, a plus-17-point net favorability rate among Democrats, simply put, they are a better brand at this point than Democrats in Congress.
sentences.zh: 美国民主社会主义者协会在民主党人中的净好感度高出17个百分点，简单来说，他们目前的品牌形象比国会里的民主党人更好。

sentences.en: But, as its electoral success grows, the organization at the heart of the movement is confronting big, unresolved questions about what it stands for,
sentences.zh: 但是，随着其选举成功的增加，处于运动核心的该组织正面临着重大且悬而未决的问题：它的立场究竟是什么，

sentences.en: what exactly its relationship to the Democratic Party should be, and what level of compromise is required to become a lasting political force.
sentences.zh: 它与民主党的关系究竟应该如何，以及要成为一股持久的政治力量需要做出何种程度的妥协。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague, political correspondent, Charlie Homans, on the rise and the limitations of the DSA.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事、政治记者查理·霍曼斯将带我们了解美国民主社会主义者协会（DSA）的崛起及其局限性。

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, August 26th.
sentences.zh: 今天是8月26日，星期三。

sentences.en: Charlie, welcome back to the show.
sentences.zh: 查理，欢迎回到节目。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请。

sentences.en: My pleasure.
sentences.zh: 我的荣幸。

sentences.en: So, by a lot of measures, this has been the summer of the Democratic Socialists.
sentences.zh: 所以，从很多方面来看，今年夏天可以说是民主社会主义者之夏。

sentences.en: And here on The Daily, we have spent a lot of time focused on Democratic Socialist candidates and the races that they are running in,
sentences.zh: 在《每日新闻》节目中，我们花了很多时间关注民主社会主义者候选人以及他们参加的竞选，

sentences.en: but not on the organization itself that's at the heart of this movement, which is the Democratic Socialists of America, the DSA.
sentences.zh: 但并没有关注这场运动核心的组织本身，也就是美国民主社会主义者协会，即DSA。

sentences.en: And so that's where you come in, Charlie, because you have spent the last few weeks reporting on the DSA and how it made this midterm election, to a large degree, about socialism.
sentences.zh: 这就是你出场的原因，查理，因为你过去几周一直在报道DSA，以及它是如何让这次中期选举在很大程度上变成了关于社会主义的议题。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: DSA has been around for a long time in various forMs.
sentences.zh: DSA以各种形式存在了很长时间。

sentences.en: But for all intents and purposes, this group wasn't really on the radar of a lot of people in politics, and I think the general public, until this past year,
sentences.zh: 但实际上，在过去一年之前，这个组织在政界乃至公众视野中并没有引起太多关注，

sentences.en: starting when Zoran Mamdani won in New York, and then continuing on through what's been a really pretty remarkable run of congressional Democratic primary wins.
sentences.zh: 从佐兰·马姆达尼在纽约获胜开始，随后又在国会民主党初选中取得了一连串相当惊人的胜利。

sentences.en: So I was interested in better understanding the organization itself, and I spent weeks talking to anyone who had talked to me in DSA, talking to the candidates,
sentences.zh: 所以我很有兴趣深入了解这个组织本身，我花了几周时间与DSA中任何愿意和我交谈的人聊天，采访候选人，

sentences.en: watching them campaigning, and came away feeling that this is a real force, a rising force in Democratic politics.
sentences.zh: 观察他们的竞选活动，最终我感觉到这是一股真正的力量，一股在民主党政治中正在崛起的力量。

sentences.en: And also that as it's growing its footprint in American politics, that it might be its own worst enemy in terms of its future.
sentences.zh: 而且我还认为，随着它在美国政治中版图的扩大，它在未来可能会成为自己最大的敌人。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And what do you mean by that exactly?
sentences.zh: 你这话具体是什么意思？

sentences.en: So you have to understand that DSA is not built as a political party.
sentences.zh: 你必须明白，DSA并不是作为一个政党建立的。

sentences.en: It exists inside of the Democratic Party these days somewhat, but it doesn't work like a party.
sentences.zh: 如今它在某种程度上存在于民主党内部，但它的运作方式并不像一个政党。

sentences.en: It's a much more fractious organization, and it has a lot of constituencies with very different ideas about how to pursue their aims in politics.
sentences.zh: 它是一个更加分裂的组织，拥有许多选民群体，他们对于如何在政治中实现目标有着非常不同的想法。

sentences.en: And as I explore deeper into the history of the organization and American socialism more generally,
sentences.zh: 当我深入探索该组织的历史以及更广泛的美国社会主义历史时，

sentences.en: I realized that these were really debates that have been happening throughout much of the history of American socialism.
sentences.zh: 我意识到这些争论实际上贯穿了美国社会主义的大部分历史。

sentences.en: And they're happening inside of DSA now in a way that is really going to affect its future as a force in American politics.
sentences.zh: 而它们现在正在DSA内部发生，这确实会影响它作为美国政治力量的未来。

sentences.en: Well, just explain then that history of American socialism that inevitably brings us to the DSA and to its inherent fractiousness.
sentences.zh: 那么，请解释一下那段不可避免地将我们引向DSA及其内在分裂性的美国社会主义历史吧。

sentences.en: So to understand DSA, I think you need to understand the early history of socialism in this country.
sentences.zh: 要理解DSA，我认为你需要了解这个国家社会主义的早期历史。

sentences.en: And that means going back to the early 1900s, which was the previous heyday of socialism here.
sentences.zh: 这意味着要回到20世纪初，那是美国社会主义上一个全盛时期。

sentences.en: You know, this is the period right after the Gilded Age when you had some Americans making just really enormous amounts of money, these sort of railroad barons, timber barons,
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是镀金时代之后的一段时期，当时一些美国人赚取了巨额财富，比如那些铁路大亨、木材大亨，

sentences.en: coal mining, that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 煤矿业等等。

sentences.en: At the same time, many Americans are working in these industries or in agriculture, and there's this huge wealth gap between the rich and everybody else.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，许多美国人在这些行业或农业中工作，富人和其他人之间存在巨大的贫富差距。

sentences.en: And this creates a lot of inevitable political reactions, people who are trying to envision a way of redistributing the wealth.
sentences.zh: 这引发了许多不可避免的政治反应，人们试图设想一种重新分配财富的方法。

sentences.en: And, you know, one thing that comes out of that eventually is this American form of socialism and specifically the Socialist Party of America,
sentences.zh: 你知道，最终产生的结果之一就是这种美国式的社会主义，特别是美国社会党，

sentences.en: which in the early 1900s was the largest and most organized socialist party in the United States.
sentences.zh: 它在20世纪初是美国最大、组织最严密的社会主义政党。

sentences.en: And socialist candidates win a fair amount of elections across the country.
sentences.zh: 社会主义候选人在全国范围内赢得了相当多的选举。

sentences.en: You know, they're not a massive movement, but socialists held assembly seats in a lot of states that would surprise you today.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们并不是一个庞大的运动，但社会主义者在许多州拥有议会席位，这在今天看来会让你感到惊讶。

sentences.en: Places like Oklahoma, Texas, the upper Midwest, socialist mayors in a lot of cities, in New York, California, really all over the place.
sentences.zh: 像俄克拉荷马州、德克萨斯州、中西部北部这些地方，在纽约、加利福尼亚等许多城市都有社会主义者市长，真的是到处都有。

sentences.en: And they really hit their pinnacle with Eugene V.
sentences.zh: 而他们的巅峰时期是在尤金·V·

sentences.en: Debs, who was the most famous socialist politician of this time period.
sentences.zh: 德布斯时期，他是那个时代最著名的社会主义政治家。

sentences.en: Fellow workers and comrades, the socialist movement is as wide as the world, and its mission is to win the world.
sentences.zh: 工友们，同志们，社会主义运动像世界一样广阔，其使命是赢得世界。

sentences.en: Debs was a union organizer and a Democratic assemblyman from Indiana who became the perennial candidate for the Socialist Party of America in five presidential elections.
sentences.zh: 德布斯是一位工会组织者，也是来自印第安纳州的民主党议员，他曾五次作为美国社会党的候选人参加总统竞选。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And really works to try to convince all these disparate groups of working class people in the United States to see themselves as a class and to see themselves with a sense of solidarity with each other.
sentences.zh: 他确实致力于说服美国所有这些不同的工人阶级群体，让他们将自己视为一个阶级，并感受到彼此之间的团结。

sentences.en: And how does Debs actually do in all these presidential elections that he runs in?
sentences.zh: 那么德布斯在他参加的所有这些总统竞选中表现如何呢？

sentences.en: So Debs topped out at 6% of the vote in 1912, which was not a lot,
sentences.zh: 德布斯在1912年的得票率最高，达到了6%，这虽然不多，

sentences.en: but was enough to make him part of the political conversation and to make socialism really part of the political conversation in the country at that time.
sentences.zh: 但足以让他参与到政治对话中，并使社会主义在当时真正成为美国政治对话的一部分。

sentences.en: And what did that look like exactly?
sentences.zh: 那具体是什么样子的？

sentences.en: How was socialism in that moment being defined in America?
sentences.zh: 当时在美国，社会主义是如何被定义的？

sentences.en: At the time, it was defined pretty clearly as public control of the workings of the economy for the benefit of the workers.
sentences.zh: 在当时，它被非常明确地定义为：为了工人的利益，对经济运作进行公共控制。

sentences.en: And in the Debs era, the socialists kind of saw this as the beginning of a real ascent into the mainstream of American politics.
sentences.zh: 在德布斯时代，社会主义者认为这是真正进入美国政治主流的开始。

sentences.en: But that's not what happened.
sentences.zh: 但事实并非如此。

sentences.en: What happened instead?
sentences.zh: 后来发生了什么？

sentences.en: So the socialists ran afoul of the government of Woodrow Wilson, specifically over World War I.
sentences.zh: 社会主义者与伍德罗·威尔逊政府发生了冲突，具体是因为第一次世界大战。

sentences.en: The socialists were very opposed to U.S.
sentences.zh: 社会主义者非常反对美国

sentences.en: involvement in the war.
sentences.zh: 卷入战争。

sentences.en: Debs encouraged young men to avoid the draft.
sentences.zh: 德布斯鼓励年轻人逃避征兵。

sentences.en: And this ended up getting him prosecuted under the Espionage Act.
sentences.zh: 这最终导致他根据《间谍法》被起诉。

sentences.en: And so by the time he runs for president in 1920, he's doing it from prison.
sentences.zh: 所以当他在1920年竞选总统时，他是在监狱里进行的。

sentences.en: Never a great situation.
sentences.zh: 那可不是什么好情况。

sentences.en: Never a great situation.
sentences.zh: 确实不是。

sentences.en: The socialists also ran into a lot of other problems kind of of their own making.
sentences.zh: 社会主义者还遇到了许多其他他们自己造成的问题。

sentences.en: They split into a number of factions in this period.
sentences.zh: 在此期间，他们分裂成了许多派系。

sentences.en: They lost a lot of ground in American politics.
sentences.zh: 他们在政治上失去了很多阵地。

sentences.en: And they were kind of a spent force really coming out of the 1920s.
sentences.zh: 到了20世纪20年代末，他们基本上已经是一股耗尽力量的势力了。

sentences.en: But another problem for them really was that actually a lot of socialist ideas that were pretty popular were advanced by non-socialist politicians in this period.
sentences.zh: 但对他们来说，另一个真正的问题是，实际上许多相当受欢迎的社会主义思想在这一时期被非社会主义政治家所推进。

sentences.en: Most importantly, FDr.
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，富兰克林·德拉诺·罗斯福（FDR）。
zh_words: 富兰克林·德拉诺·罗斯福

sentences.en: Who borrowed a lot of what was thought of as democratic socialist economic policy as part of his New Deal to help America out of the Great Depression.
sentences.zh: 他借用了许多被认为是民主社会主义的经济政策，作为其“新政”的一部分，以帮助美国走出大萧条。

sentences.en: Only a foolish optimist can deny the dark realities of the moment.
sentences.zh: 只有愚蠢的乐观主义者才会否认当下的黑暗现实。

sentences.en: This is another moment, again, when there's a huge wealth gap in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 这是另一个时刻，美国再次出现了巨大的贫富差距。

sentences.en: Farmers find no markets for their produce and the savings of many years in thousands of families are gone.
sentences.zh: 农民找不到农产品的市场，成千上万个家庭多年的积蓄化为乌有。

sentences.en: And people see capitalism as really a broken system.
sentences.zh: 人们认为资本主义是一个真正破碎的体系。

sentences.en: Our greatest primary task is to put people to work in part by direct recruiting by the government itself.
sentences.zh: 我们最重要的首要任务是让人们重返工作岗位，部分通过政府直接招募来实现。

sentences.en: And so FDR pushes through things like federal employment programs, big public works projects, Social Security.
sentences.zh: 因此，罗斯福推行了联邦就业计划、大型公共工程项目、社会保障等措施。

sentences.en: This Social Security measure gives at least some protection against the loss of a job and against poverty-stricken old age.
sentences.zh: 这项社会保障措施至少提供了一些针对失业和贫困晚年的保护。

sentences.en: These were ideas that were very similar to what socialists had been advocating for.
sentences.zh: 这些想法与社会主义者一直倡导的非常相似。

sentences.en: And it really kind of stole a lot of the fire from American socialism to have these enacted by a progressive democratic presidency.
sentences.zh: 由进步的民主党总统颁布这些政策，确实在很大程度上削弱了美国社会主义运动的势头。

sentences.en: I'm curious if FDR saw what he was doing as any form of socialism and if anyone else in American politics at that time called it socialism.
sentences.zh: 我很好奇罗斯福是否将自己的所作所为视为某种形式的社会主义，以及当时美国政坛是否有人称其为社会主义。

sentences.en: FDR saw himself as a reformer of capitalism.
sentences.zh: 罗斯福将自己视为资本主义的改革者。

sentences.en: So he was happy to borrow a lot of these ideas that, again, we would, in another context, consider socialist,
sentences.zh: 所以他很乐意借用许多在其他背景下会被认为是社会主义的想法，

sentences.en: but as a way of correcting the capitalist system rather than replacing it.
sentences.zh: 但他是将其作为一种修正资本主义体系而非取代它的手段。

sentences.en: We'll try to give you new...
sentences.zh: 我们将尝试给你新的……

sentences.en: And in fact, he pushed back against the idea that this was socialiSt.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他反驳了这是社会主义的说法。

sentences.en: Sometimes they will call it fascism, and sometimes communism, and sometimes socialism.
sentences.zh: 有时他们称之为法西斯主义，有时是共产主义，有时是社会主义。

sentences.en: But in so doing, they are trying to make very complex and theoretical something that is really very simple and very practical.
sentences.zh: 但这样做，他们是在试图把非常简单和实际的东西变得非常复杂和理论化。

sentences.en: And the reason FDR is careful not to call this socialism is because of what's happening around the world at this time.
sentences.zh: 罗斯福之所以小心翼翼地不称其为社会主义，是因为当时世界各地正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: You know, the Russian Revolution has happened.
sentences.zh: 你知道，俄国革命已经发生了。

sentences.en: The Soviet Union's been born.
sentences.zh: 苏联已经诞生。

sentences.en: This is the first country that embraces communism.
sentences.zh: 这是第一个拥抱共产主义的国家。

sentences.en: Now, communism is a much more radical and, in the Soviet Union, undemocratic system evolving from socialism, one that many American socialists reject.
sentences.zh: 现在，共产主义是一个比社会主义更激进、在苏联更不民主的体系，许多美国社会主义者对此表示拒绝。

sentences.en: But this has led to all these ideologies being seen in the United States as foreign and threatening in a way that they weren't necessarily before.
sentences.zh: 但这导致所有这些意识形态在美国被视为外来的、具有威胁性的，这在以前未必如此。

sentences.en: But as we saw with FDR, some socialist ideas can still find their way into the mainstream if they're packaged right.
sentences.zh: 但正如我们在罗斯福身上看到的，如果包装得当，一些社会主义思想仍然可以进入主流。

sentences.en: And so I think the New Deal sets up what really becomes the central question that socialists confront in this country throughout the rest of the 20th century and into the 21st century.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为“新政”提出了社会主义者在整个20世纪乃至21世纪所面临的核心问题。

sentences.en: Which is, are you content seeing ideas that you broadly support that emerge from your politics being enacted at a large scale,

sentences.en: So with that in mind, where does this movement go after the New Deal ends up, to a degree, stealing a lot of socialists' thunder?
sentences.zh: 那么考虑到这一点，在“新政”在一定程度上抢走了社会主义者的风头之后，这场运动走向了何方？

sentences.en: He decides to form a new socialist organization called Democratic Socialists of America.

sentences.zh: 他成为了该组织现代演变中一个非常关键的人物。

sentences.en: And what democratic socialism is about is saying that it is immoral and wrong that the top one tenth of one percent in this country own almost as much wealth as the bottom 90 percent.

sentences.en: And he also sort of points this movement forward towards the real policy focuses that will continue to define DSA going forward.
sentences.zh: 他也引导这场运动关注那些将继续定义DSA未来发展的真正政策重点。

sentences.en: We should have health care for every man, woman and child as a right.

sentences.en: No, I don't.
sentences.zh: 不，我不认为。

sentences.zh: 他确实利用了金融危机引发的民粹主义愤怒。

sentences.zh: 这场竞选的意义在于，我们能否动员民众从少数亿万富翁手中夺回政府，并创造出我们能够且应该拥有的充满活力的民主。

sentences.en: And overall, this message that the establishment has rigged the system against working people and working people need to take their power back.
sentences.zh: 总的来说，这种信息是：建制派操纵了体制来对付劳动人民，而劳动人民需要夺回他们的权力。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: the post-Gilded Age era and the Great Depression,
sentences.zh: 镀金时代之后和经济大萧条时期，

sentences.zh: 那两个时期国家的贫富差距都非常巨大，美国劳动者感到被资本主义制度抛弃和背叛。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And obviously, people on the left are really drawing those connections at the time, you know, pointing to the resonances with the Gilded Age, Great Depression.
sentences.zh: 显然，当时左翼人士确实在建立这些联系，你知道，指出与镀金时代、大萧条的共鸣。

sentences.en: But for the socialists, what Bernie did that was really important was show that self-identified socialists could actually do quite well in a democratic primary.
sentences.zh: 但对于社会主义者来说，伯尼所做的真正重要的事情是证明了自称社会主义者的人实际上可以在民主党初选中表现得相当不错。

sentences.zh: 你必须记住，在此之前，社会主义在美国政治中一直是一个非常禁忌的词，而且已经持续了很长一段时间。

sentences.en: And Bernie kind of reclaimed this word as something that you could actually run on as a left-wing candidate and said, yeah,
sentences.zh: 伯尼以某种方式重新定义了这个词，使它成为你可以作为左翼候选人竞选时使用的标签，他说，是的，

sentences.en: I am a socialist and really embraced this label very directly in a way that people prior to 2016, I think,

sentences.zh: 而伯尼所做的就是证明这根本不是事实。

sentences.en: And his candidacy becomes this real movement and draws all these people to his cause.
sentences.zh: 他的参选成为了一场真正的运动，并吸引了所有这些人加入他的事业。

sentences.en: And after the election, all these people are kind of out there asking, what do we do with this energy and these ideas?
sentences.zh: 选举结束后，所有这些人都在问，我们该如何利用这些精力和想法？

sentences.zh: 他们想出的一个重要答案是：加入DSA。

sentences.en: So this is a massive increase in not just the size of the organization, but the demographics of it.
sentences.zh: 所以这不仅是组织规模的巨大增长，也是人口结构的巨大变化。

sentences.en: You know, this had been a much kind of old, tweety group of people for the most part before this moment.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在此之前，这基本上是一个非常老派、喜欢在推特上发牢骚的群体。

sentences.en: And by their own statistics, the median age of a DSA member after 2016 drops from 68 to 33.
sentences.zh: 根据他们自己的统计数据，2016年后DSA成员的平均年龄从68岁降至33岁。

sentences.en: And so these people do a lot of things inside of DSA.
sentences.zh: 所以这些人开始在DSA内部做很多事情。

sentences.zh: 他们在城市、大学校园里建立新的分部，这些地方以前都没有DSA分部。

sentences.en: And they start organizing campaigns and they start running for office themselves.
sentences.zh: 他们开始组织竞选活动，并亲自参加竞选。

We launched this campaign because no one was clearly and authentically talking about issues like the corrupting role of money in politics.

sentences.en: And for DSA, that's a bigger deal than it might be in the Democratic Party or the Republican Party, where there's a sort of understanding that, like,

sentences.en: With DSA,
sentences.zh: 而对于DSA，

sentences.en: so much of the kind of foundational idea of the post-Bernie DSA was that this was an organization that was going to produce a different kind of left-wing candidate that was really going to be accountable to something outside of their own career interests,
sentences.zh: 后伯尼时代DSA的基本理念很大程度上在于，这是一个将产生不同类型左翼候选人的组织，他们将真正对自身职业利益之外的事物负责，

sentences.en: outside of the Democratic Party.

sentences.en: And AOC kind of runs afoul of that because she does sort of tack away from DSA on some things.

sentences.zh: 变化程度如何，这非常值得商榷。

sentences.en: It is the case that the sort of median DSA voter was a college-educated professional who was probably downwardly economically mobile.
sentences.zh: 事实是，DSA的中间选民通常是受过大学教育的专业人士，他们可能在经济上处于下行趋势。

sentences.en: Not a picture of the working class, much less the working class of color in this country.
sentences.zh: 这并不是工人阶级的写照，更不用说这个国家的有色人种工人阶级了。

sentences.en: That has sort of evolved over time, though.
sentences.zh: 不过，这种情况随着时间的推移已经有所演变。

sentences.en: I mean, it's worth noting that, you know, Mumdani won with a bigger map than previous DSA candidates in New York.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，值得注意的是，你知道，穆姆达尼（Mumdani）在纽约赢得竞选时，其选民版图比之前的DSA候选人更大。

sentences.en: Donovan McKinney won a plurality black district in Detroit.
sentences.zh: 多诺万·麦金尼（Donovan McKinney）在底特律的一个黑人占多数的选区获胜。

sentences.en: And you also saw a pretty different pattern of DSA support, at least in the exit polls, from Angie Nixon's primary win in Florida.
sentences.zh: 而且你还看到，至少在出口民调中，安吉·尼克松（Angie Nixon）在佛罗里达州的初选胜利中，DSA的支持模式也大不相同。

sentences.en: So there is reason to think that the picture is not quite as totally fixed as DSA's critics would have it.
sentences.zh: 所以有理由认为，情况并不像DSA的批评者所说的那样完全固定不变。

sentences.en: Well,
sentences.zh: 嗯，

sentences.en: let's now turn from the DSA as a fractious organization to the Democratic Party itself and how its leaders are thinking about this DSA moment and this DSA insurgency that's taking out some of its members.
sentences.zh: 现在让我们从作为一个分裂组织的DSA转向民主党本身，以及它的领导层是如何看待这个DSA时刻，以及这个正在淘汰其部分成员的DSA叛乱的。

sentences.en: And its preferred candidates.
sentences.zh: 以及它所青睐的候选人。

sentences.en: What is the broad feeling among the Democratic Party's leadership about whether the DSA is something that they can harness, whether it's something they should embrace,
sentences.zh: 民主党领导层对于DSA是否是可以利用的力量，是否应该拥抱它，

sentences.en: or if the DSA is something to be feared?
sentences.zh: 或者DSA是否是令人恐惧的对象，有着怎样的普遍感受？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that's a very live debate in the Democratic Party right now.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为这在目前的民主党内部是一个非常活跃的辩论。

sentences.en: I mean, you see people like Gavin Newsom, who is sort of arguing that DSA should be welcomed into the Democratic coalition,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你看到像加文·纽森（Gavin Newsom）这样的人，他主张应该欢迎DSA加入民主党联盟，

sentences.en: and that the party should really be in the business of addition and not subtraction, as he put it.
sentences.zh: 正如他所说，党应该致力于做加法而不是减法。

sentences.en: You know, this is an energized constituency that has really tapped an energy, and particularly a younger energy, that the Democratic Party has really struggled to tap.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是一个充满活力的选民群体，他们确实激发了一种能量，特别是民主党一直难以触及的年轻人的能量。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Why would you turn your back on that?
sentences.zh: 你为什么要背弃这一点呢？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Like, they have sort of figured out how to appeal to these people who, you know, there's really kind of broad discontent with the state of the country right now.
sentences.zh: 他们似乎已经找到了吸引这些人的方法，你知道，目前人们对国家现状普遍存在不满。

sentences.en: And this is basically a net positive for the Democratic Party, this line of argument goes.
sentences.zh: 这种论点认为，这对民主党来说基本上是一个净收益。

sentences.en: If you can figure out how to bring these people in as real coalitional partners, that, you know, this is really to the good of the broader party.
sentences.zh: 如果你能想出如何让这些人成为真正的联盟伙伴，那么，这对整个党来说确实是有利的。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: But critics of the DSA, kind of a mix of some of the reform-minded Democrats and also a lot of people who are really just ideological moderates, you know,
sentences.zh: 但是DSA的批评者，包括一些改革派民主党人和许多纯粹的意识形态温和派，你知道，

sentences.en: they argue that this is a fundamental misunderstanding of the DSA and its project.
sentences.zh: 他们认为这是对DSA及其项目的根本性误解。

sentences.en: That this is not an organization that sees itself as part of that coalition.
sentences.zh: 认为这不是一个将自己视为该联盟一部分的组织。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: That their relationship with the Democratic Party is really not additive.
sentences.zh: 他们与民主党的关系实际上并不是相加的。

sentences.en: You know, it's actually parasitic.
sentences.zh: 你知道，实际上是寄生的。

sentences.en: Meaning what?
sentences.zh: 这是什么意思？

sentences.en: Well, to this point, they have not proven capable of flipping really any seats anywhere in this country.
sentences.zh: 嗯，到目前为止，他们还没有证明自己有能力在这个国家的任何地方翻转任何席位。

sentences.en: The only places they've won in elections have been very safely blue districts or cities, which they've succeeded in making more lefty than they were before.
sentences.zh: 他们在选举中获胜的唯一地方是非常安全的蓝色选区或城市，他们成功地使这些地方比以前更左倾了。

sentences.en: And so the argument that is sort of most pointedly made about them is what exactly are you guys doing for us?
sentences.zh: 所以关于他们最尖锐的论点是：你们到底为我们做了什么？

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: You talk about revitalizing the Democratic Party, but you can't do anything you want to do without winning congressional majorities,
sentences.zh: 你们谈论振兴民主党，但如果不赢得国会多数席位，你们什么都做不了，

sentences.en: Senate majorities that you have zero demonstrated ability to do.
sentences.zh: 你们在赢得参议院多数席位方面没有任何证明过的能力。

sentences.en: So that argument is basically if you're only replacing Democrats in Democratic districts with Democratic Socialists, how are you advancing the cause of winning swing districts?
sentences.zh: 所以这个论点基本上是：如果你只是在民主党选区用民主社会主义者取代民主党人，你如何推动赢得摇摆选区的目标？

sentences.en: How are you growing the majorities in the House and in the Senate that would actually make it possible for your agenda or any version of the Democratic agenda to be enacted in Congress?
sentences.zh: 你如何增加众议院和参议院的多数席位，从而使你的议程或任何版本的民主党议程能够在国会中得以实施？

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And when you ask DSA leaders about this, they will make an argument that they are advancing popular political ideas,
sentences.zh: 当你问DSA领导人这个问题时，他们会辩称他们正在推动受欢迎的政治理念，

sentences.en: ideas that if they are actually implemented or embraced by a party, will bring out new voters who have not voted before and change the math and politics in a fundamental way.
sentences.zh: 如果这些理念真的被一个政党实施或采纳，将会吸引以前从未投票的新选民，并从根本上改变政治格局。

sentences.en: I would say that that is entirely waiting to be proven, that there's really no evidence of their ability to do that.
sentences.zh: 我会说这完全有待证明，实际上没有任何证据表明他们有能力做到这一点。

sentences.en: I think that it's fair to say the burden of proof rests with the DSA on that.
sentences.zh: 我认为可以公平地说，证明的责任在于DSA。

sentences.en: If these people ever do get in charge, we might as well turn out the lights and make sure the cat's inside and go to bed because it's over.
sentences.zh: 如果这些人真的掌权了，我们还不如关灯，把猫关好，然后去睡觉，因为一切都结束了。

sentences.en: These people are crazy as a bed bug.
sentences.zh: 这些人疯得像臭虫一样。

sentences.en: And in the meantime, Republicans clearly see these same ideas as a massive liability for the Democratic Party.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，共和党人显然认为这些相同的理念对民主党来说是一个巨大的负担。

sentences.en: The DSA is calling the shots.
sentences.zh: DSA正在发号施令。

sentences.en: And what you see is a party that is tilting so far left.
sentences.zh: 你所看到的是一个正在向左倾斜得如此厉害的政党。

sentences.en: They're not just running on different policies.
sentences.zh: 他们不仅仅是在推行不同的政策。

sentences.en: They are running to destroy the country.
sentences.zh: 他们是在竞选摧毁这个国家。

sentences.en: They've been pointing to the DSA all summer quite happily and saying, look at all these policies they're throwing out there.
sentences.zh: 他们整个夏天都很高兴地指着DSA说，看看他们抛出的所有这些政策。

sentences.en: So if we talk about abolishing prisons, then does that make society better?
sentences.zh: 所以如果我们谈论废除监狱，那会让社会变得更好吗？

sentences.en: I mean, is there anybody that should be incarcerated?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有谁应该被监禁吗？

sentences.en: I mean, rapists, child predators, murderers?
sentences.zh: 我是说，强奸犯、虐待儿童者、杀人犯？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So the long term plan, when we think about most people who are in prison, they are mostly in prison for crimes of poverty.
sentences.zh: 所以长期的计划是，当我们想到大多数在监狱里的人时，他们大多是因为贫困犯罪而入狱的。

sentences.en: But that's not what I'm talking about.
sentences.zh: 但那不是我在谈论的。

sentences.en: I'm talking about the really, you know, like the murders.
sentences.zh: 我在谈论的是，你知道，比如谋杀犯。

sentences.en: You know, Fox News has on the co-chairs of the DSA to sort of defend this platform live on the air.
sentences.zh: 你知道，福克斯新闻邀请DSA的联合主席在直播中为这个纲领辩护。

sentences.en: OK, but you do think some people need to be locked away from society.
sentences.zh: 好吧，但你确实认为有些人需要被关起来，远离社会。

sentences.en: Some people are not able to be functional members of society.
sentences.zh: 有些人无法成为社会的正常成员。

sentences.en: That's true.
sentences.zh: 那是真的。

sentences.en: But what does that look like to keep the rest of us safe?
sentences.zh: 但为了保障我们其余人的安全，那会是什么样子？

sentences.en: You know, we're talking about safety.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们在谈论安全。

sentences.en: Yeah, there's a sense that the more out there aspects of what DSA wants to do is going to be a real liability for not just DSA candidates,
sentences.zh: 是的，有一种感觉，DSA想要做的事情中那些更激进的方面，不仅对DSA候选人来说是一个真正的负担，

sentences.en: but for Democrats more broadly if this becomes really associated with the party brand.
sentences.zh: 如果这真的与党的品牌联系在一起，对整个民主党来说也是如此。

sentences.en: Instead of defunding, decriminalizing, open borders, we have run that play and gotten our butts kicked.
sentences.zh: 而不是削减经费、去刑事化、开放边境，我们已经玩过那套把戏，结果被踢得屁滚尿流。

sentences.en: We don't need to do it a second time to see if the movie turns out any different.
sentences.zh: 我们不需要再做一次来看看电影结局是否会有所不同。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So in that sense, Democratic Party leaders do have something to fear here with the DSA.
sentences.zh: 所以从这个意义上说，民主党领导人确实有理由对DSA感到恐惧。

sentences.en: But it strikes me that those Democratic leaders might not really have a choice at this point.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，这些民主党领导人在这一点上可能真的别无选择。

sentences.en: The DSA is strong.
sentences.zh: DSA很强大。

sentences.en: Its strength is growing.
sentences.zh: 它的力量正在增长。

sentences.en: It seems like it's here to stay.
sentences.zh: 它似乎会一直存在下去。

sentences.en: And I say that because we have a pretty recent model of this happening in our politics on the other side of the aisle.
sentences.zh: 我之所以这么说，是因为我们在政治光谱的另一端有一个最近发生的类似模式。

sentences.en: And here I'm thinking about the rise of the Tea Party on the American right back in 2009, 2010.
sentences.zh: 这里我想到的是2009年、2010年美国右翼茶党（Tea Party）的兴起。

sentences.en: Obviously, the Tea Party stands for something very different than the DSA.
sentences.zh: 显然，茶党所代表的与DSA非常不同。

sentences.en: It's an anti-government movement, but its origins feel quite similar to what we're seeing now, this insurgency that campaigns against and takes out incumbents.
sentences.zh: 它是一场反政府运动，但其起源与我们现在所看到的非常相似，这种反对并淘汰现任者的叛乱。

sentences.en: And then its ideals slowly but surely become the ideology of the entire party, the Republican Party in that case.
sentences.zh: 然后它的理想慢慢地但肯定地成为了整个政党，即那种情况下的共和党的意识形态。

sentences.en: Is that a fair comparison?
sentences.zh: 这是一个公平的比较吗？

sentences.en: And is the Tea Party a potential blueprint for the DSA to follow?
sentences.zh: 茶党是DSA可以效仿的潜在蓝图吗？

sentences.en: That's an interesting question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个有趣的问题。

sentences.en: And I think the two comparisons that are always sort of there to make to DSA, although people on both sides of American politics would no doubt vigorously dispute these,
sentences.zh: 我认为关于DSA总是可以进行的两个比较，尽管美国政治两边的人无疑会强烈反驳这些，

sentences.en: is whether it is more like the Tea Party or more like MAGA.
sentences.zh: 是它更像茶党还是更像“让美国再次伟大”（MAGA）。

sentences.en: You know, the Tea Party, as you say, was a movement that arose in response to the financial crisis, more importantly, to Barack Obama's first presidency,
sentences.zh: 你知道，正如你所说，茶党是一场为应对金融危机，更重要的是为应对巴拉克·奥巴马（Barack Obama）的第一个总统任期而兴起的运动，

sentences.en: and did much better than DSA in terms of seizing ground in Congress very quickly.
sentences.zh: 在国会迅速抢占地盘方面，他们比美国民主社会主义者协会（DSA）做得好得多。

sentences.en: They won dozens of seats in 2010.
sentences.zh: 他们在2010年赢得了数十个席位。

sentences.en: And they unquestionably succeeded in pushing the Republican Party to the right and establishing themselves as a power center within that party.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，他们成功地将共和党推向了右翼，并确立了自己作为该党内部权力中心的地位。

sentences.en: Along the way, they did not achieve everything that they set out to achieve and were in many respects sort of assimilated into the Republican Party.
sentences.zh: 在此过程中，他们并没有实现所有既定目标，在许多方面甚至被共和党同化了。

sentences.en: You know, that's one scenario.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是一种设想。

sentences.en: The other scenario is that DSA is something more like MAGA.
sentences.zh: 另一种设想是，DSA更像是“让美国再次伟大”（MAGA）运动。

sentences.en: A movement that sort of initially establishment Republicans kind of made fun of and didn't take seriously and then accommodated, and then it eventually devoured the party.
sentences.zh: 起初，建制派共和党人对这种运动嗤之以鼻，并不当回事，后来却选择了妥协，最终该运动吞噬了整个政党。

sentences.en: That was obviously only really possible with the presence of somebody like Donald Trump, who doesn't exist in DSA.
sentences.zh: 显然，这只有在像唐纳德·特朗普这样的人存在时才有可能实现，而DSA中并没有这样的人。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: At the moment, the DSA does not have that, a single unifying national leader who can wrangle all of its factions.
sentences.zh: 目前，DSA还没有这样一位能够统领其所有派系的单一全国性领袖。

sentences.en: In fact, its structure seems to put those factions very much at the center of the organization.
sentences.zh: 事实上，其组织结构似乎将这些派系置于组织的核心位置。

sentences.en: And that makes me wonder, how does DSA move from insurgency to something more enduring in our politics?
sentences.zh: 这让我不禁思考，DSA如何才能从一场叛乱运动转变为我们政治中更持久的力量？

sentences.en: Well, the thing about DSA is that in spite of all of its organizational problems, some of its chapters, particularly New York,
sentences.zh: 嗯，关于DSA，尽管它存在各种组织问题，但它的一些分部，特别是纽约分部，

sentences.en: have succeeded in producing really dynamic, successful politicians.
sentences.zh: 已经成功培养出了非常有活力、非常成功的政治家。

sentences.en: They've produced Mamdani.
sentences.zh: 他们培养了马姆达尼（Mamdani）。

sentences.en: They've produced AOC.
sentences.zh: 他们培养了AOC（亚历山德里娅·奥卡西奥-科尔特斯）。
zh_words: 亚历山德里娅·奥卡西奥

sentences.en: And that's why I think people who both want to see the DSA succeed on the national level and people who are very concerned about DSA agree that the real game changer in this,
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我认为，无论是希望看到DSA在全国层面取得成功的人，还是对DSA非常担忧的人，都同意这一点：真正的转折点在于，

sentences.en: and possibly the necessary game changer from DSA's standpoint is a presidential candidacy, a strong contender who comes out of DSA, who isn't just a socialist like Bernie Sanders,
sentences.zh: 从DSA的角度来看，这可能是必要的转折点，那就是总统候选人资格，一位来自DSA的强有力竞争者，他不仅仅像伯尼·桑德斯那样是个社会主义者，

sentences.en: but is actually a DSA candidate.
sentences.zh: 而是真正的DSA候选人。

sentences.en: You know, that is something that I think everybody agrees could really transform the place of DSA in American politics.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我认为大家都同意，这确实可以改变DSA在美国政治中的地位。

sentences.en: I think I know why that will transform the DSA and its place in politics, but just explain why it will be so important that a homegrown DSA presidential candidate
sentences.zh: 我想我知道为什么这会改变DSA及其在政治中的地位，但请解释一下，为什么一位本土的DSA总统候选人

sentences.en: would be the game changer.
sentences.zh: 会成为那个转折点，这如此重要？

sentences.en: I mean, if you look at the arc of American political history, ideas that are coming in from pretty far outside of the mainstream of politics
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你审视美国政治史的轨迹，那些来自政治主流之外的理念，

sentences.en: struggle to colonize those politics from the ground up.
sentences.zh: 往往很难从基层开始去殖民化这些政治。

sentences.en: What is really invaluable is to have a head of state or even a strong presidential candidate
sentences.zh: 真正无价的是拥有一位国家元首，甚至是一位强有力的总统候选人，

sentences.en: bring those ideas in a very high profile and central way in front of the majority of the
sentences.zh: 以一种非常引人注目且核心的方式，将这些理念呈现在大多数

sentences.en: American population and sort of acclimatize them to these ideas, normalize these ideas.
sentences.zh: 美国民众面前，让他们适应这些理念，使这些理念正常化。

sentences.en: FDR as president did that with these progressive policy ideas that, again, we might in another context have associated with socialism.
sentences.zh: 富兰克林·罗斯福（FDR）作为总统，用这些进步政策理念做到了这一点，而这些理念，在另一种语境下，我们可能会将其与社会主义联系起来。

sentences.en: Ronald Reagan did the same thing with conservatism.
sentences.zh: 罗纳德·里根在保守主义方面也做了同样的事情。

sentences.en: Conservatism was a marginal movement in the Republican Party for years, and it was really sort of the concerted efforts of Reagan that really brought that
sentences.zh: 保守主义在共和党内曾多年处于边缘地位，正是里根的共同努力，才真正将其

sentences.en: not just into the mainstream of American politics, but made it really the sort of unconquerable like doctrine inside of the Republican Party eventually.
sentences.zh: 不仅带入了美国政治的主流，而且最终使其成为了共和党内某种不可战胜的教条。

sentences.en: Donald Trump in his own way has clearly done that with a lot of ideas that were considered wildly outside of American politics a decade ago.
sentences.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普以他自己的方式，显然也用许多十年前被认为完全游离于美国政治之外的理念做到了这一点。

sentences.en: There's really no substitute for a politician at that national level who is able to just sort of center a political program day in and day out.
sentences.zh: 对于一位能够日复一日地专注于政治纲领的全国级政治家来说，确实没有替代品。

sentences.en: So just game that out.
sentences.zh: 所以，让我们推演一下。

sentences.en: Pretend for a moment that there is a very successful Democratic Socialist presidential campaign, and that candidate, maybe it's AOC, maybe it's somebody else, wins the nomination,
sentences.zh: 假设一下，有一场非常成功的民主社会主义总统竞选，而那位候选人，也许是AOC，也许是别人，赢得了提名，

sentences.en: and suddenly DSA is the national face of a Democratic Party.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，DSA成为了民主党的全国门面。

sentences.en: I think if you have a Democratic Socialist running as the Democratic nominee in a presidential election,

sentences.en: you end up with a referendum on socialism that we have never had in this country.
sentences.zh: 你最终会得到一场我们国家从未有过的关于社会主义的全民公投。

sentences.en: In one scenario, this normalizes the ideas that socialists have been arguing for in this country for over a century.
sentences.zh: 在一种设想中，这使社会主义者在这个国家争论了一个多世纪的理念正常化了。

sentences.en: This word that has for years had this taboo around it loses the kind of scariness with even a general electorate that is still, by the polls, wary of the idea of socialism.
sentences.zh: 这个多年来一直带有禁忌色彩的词，即使在民调显示仍对社会主义理念持谨慎态度的普通选民中，也失去了那种可怕感。

sentences.en: The other scenario is that this functionally destroys the Democratic Party for years and its ability to win an election.
sentences.zh: 另一种设想是，这在功能上摧毁了民主党多年来的选举获胜能力。

sentences.en: It's saddled with this label that remains unpopular, and that's what people think of when they think of Democrats.
sentences.zh: 它背负着这个仍然不受欢迎的标签，而这正是人们想到民主党时所想到的。

sentences.en: And so this is a conversation that's very live right now inside of the DSA.
sentences.zh: 所以，这正是DSA内部目前非常活跃的对话。

sentences.en: What kind of compromises are going to be required to make a Democratic Socialist candidate tolerable to the majority of Americans?
sentences.zh: 为了让大多数美国人能够容忍民主社会主义候选人，需要做出什么样的妥协？

sentences.en: And are they willing to make those compromises?
sentences.zh: 他们愿意做出这些妥协吗？

sentences.en: Or does all this end in big public ruptures, you know, that take the DSA from this moment of ascendancy to a moment of irrelevance
sentences.zh: 还是这一切最终会以巨大的公开决裂告终，你知道，让DSA从这一上升时刻走向无关紧要的时刻，

sentences.en: that socialists have experienced throughout most of their history in this country?
sentences.zh: 就像社会主义者在这个国家的大部分历史中所经历的那样？

sentences.en: We don't know.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道。

sentences.en: And I think we've seen the beginning of this conversation in the midterms, but it's really only the beginning of this conversation.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们在中期选举中看到了这场对话的开始，但这确实只是这场对话的开始。
